title: 2020年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 Picture this: You're at a movie theater food stand loading up on snacks. You have a choice of a small, medium or large soda. The small is $3.50 and the large is $5.50. It's a tough decision: The small size may not last you through the whole movie, but $5.50 for some sugary drink seems ridiculous. But there's a third option, a medium soda for $5.25. Medium may be the perfect amount of soda for you, but the large is only a quarter more. If you're like most people, you end up buying the large (and taking a bathroom break midshow).

P2 If you're wondering who would buy the medium soda, the answer is almost no one. In fact, there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy(诱饵), making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small.

P3 I have written about this peculiarity in human nature before with my friend Dan Ariely, who studied this phenomenon extensively after noticing pricing for subscriptions(订阅) to The Economist. The digital subscription was $59, the print subscription was $125, and the print plus digital subscription was also $125. No one in their right mind would buy the print subscription when you could get digital as well for the same price, so why was it even an option? Ariely ran an experiment and found that when only the two "real" choices were offered, more people chose the less-expensive digital subscription. But the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option.

P4 Brain scientists call this effect "asymmetric dominance" and it means that people gravitate toward the choice nearest a clearly inferior option. Marketing professors call it the decoy effect, which is certainly easier to remember. Lucky for consumers, almost no one in the business community understands it.

P5 The decoy effect works because of the way our brains assign value when making choices. Value is almost never absolute; rather, we decide an object's value relative to our other choices. If more options are introduced, the value equation changes.

questions.q: Why does the author ask us to imagine buying food in the movie theater?
options: To illustrate people's peculiar shopping behavior.
To illustrate the increasing variety of snacks there.
To show how hard it can be to choose a drink there.
To show how popular snacks are among movie fans.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does the author ask us to imagine buying food问的是作者为什么设置这个例子， 不是问例子本身说了什么，属于例证目的题。

【拆句】Why does the author ask us to imagine buying food in the movie theater?是一个why 引导的特殊疑问句，主干为Why does the author ask us，to imagine buying food是ask 的宾语补足语，in the movie theater作地点状语修饰imagine。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. Why does the author ask us to imagine buying food in the movie theater? A) To illustrate people's peculiar shopping behavior. B) To illustrate the increasing variety of snacks there. C) To show how hard it can be to choose a drink there. D) To show how popular snacks are among movie fans.

【定位】If you're wondering who would buy the medium soda, the answer is almost no one. In fact, there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small. 如果你在想谁会去买中杯可乐，答案是几乎没人。事实上，营销部门很可能是故意把中杯定 价为诱饵，让你更倾向于买大杯而不是小杯。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small ↔people's peculiar shopping behavior Picture this: You're at a movie theater food stand ↔To illustrate 预判到答案是"展示异常购物行为"，选项里只有To illustrate people's peculiar shopping behavior同时覆盖illustrate（举例目的）和peculiar shopping behavior （异常购物行为），与预判完全吻合。 B) 无中生有 the increasing variety of snacks说的是零食"种类的增多"，但原文从头到尾只谈大中小 三种可乐的定价心理，根本没有讨论零食种类多寡。 C) 偷换概念 how hard it can be to choose a drink说的是"选饮料有多难"。原文It's a tough decision确实承认决定难，但这只是引出诱饵效应的铺垫，作者的真正意图不是讲选择 之难，而是讲选择被操纵；选项把铺垫当成目的，是偷换。 D) 无中生有 how popular snacks are among movie fans说的是"零食在影迷中多受欢迎"，原文完 全没有谈零食的受欢迎程度，也没把读者定义为movie fans。 中杯汽水为什么这样定价? A) 为了吸引更多顾客购买它。 B) 为了显示价格与分量相匹配。 C) 为了确保顾客饮用适量的汽水。 D) 为了让顾客相信他们得到了实惠。

questions.q: Why is the medium soda priced the way it is?
options: To attract more customers to buy it.
To show the price matches the amount.
To ensure customers drink the right amount of soda.
To make customers believe they are getting a bargain.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why is the medium soda priced the way it is问的是文中已明示的因果，是对原文具体信 息的再现，属于细节题。

【拆句】Why is the medium soda priced the way it is?主干为被动结构the medium soda is priced，the way it is是方式状语从句简写（=in the way that it is priced），整体问的 是"为何如此定价"。考生需读懂被动语态，把priced还原成"被定价"。 52. Why is the medium soda priced the way it is? A) To attract more customers to buy it. B) To show the price matches the amount. C) To ensure customers drink the right amount of soda. D) To make customers believe they are getting a bargain.

【定位】In fact, there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small. 事实上，营销部门很可能是故意把中杯定价为诱饵，让你更倾向于买大杯而不是小杯。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 To attract more customers to buy it说的是"吸引更多顾客来买中杯"，但If you're wondering who would buy the medium soda, the answer is almost no one明确告 诉我们中杯定价的目的恰恰不是为了卖中杯本身。 B) 无中生有 To show the price matches the amount说的是"展示价格与分量相符"，但原文从未声 称中杯价格合理，反而暗示这种定价是营销操纵。 C) 偷换概念 To ensure customers drink the right amount of soda说的是"确保顾客喝合适的量"， 体现的是关怀消费者健康的善意动机；原文中营销部门的动机是purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy，即操纵性的，与善意正相反。 D) ✓ 正确 purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small ↔To make customers believe they are getting a bargain Medium may be the perfect amount of soda for you, but the large is only a quarter more ↔ getting a bargain 预判答案是"让顾客觉得大杯划算/占便宜"，make customers believe they are getting a bargain里getting a bargain正是"占便宜"的标准说法，与预判精准匹配。 我们从Dan Ariely的实验中了解到什么? A) 价格较低的商品吸引更多顾客。 B) The Economist的促销策略有效。 C) The Economist的印刷版最终卖得最好。 D) 更多读者选择数字版而非印刷版。

questions.q: What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment?
options: Lower-priced goods attract more customers.
The Economist's promotional strategy works.
The Economist's print edition turns out to sell the best.
More readers choose the digital over the print edition.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment问的是实验本身揭示了什么客观事实， 是对原文的转述，属细节题。

【拆句】What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment?是what引导的特殊疑问句，主干为we learn，from Dan Ariely's experiment为状语。结构直白，无陷阱。 53. What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment? A) Lower-priced goods attract more customers. B) The Economist's promotional strategy works. C) The Economist's print edition turns out to sell the best. D) More readers choose the digital over the print edition.

【定位】Ariely ran an experiment and found that when only the two "real" choices were offered, more people chose the less-expensive digital subscription. But the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option. Ariely做了一个实验发现：只提供两个"真实"选项时，更多人选了便宜的纯数字订阅。但加 入那个糟糕的选项后，人们更倾向于选更贵的纸质加数字组合订阅。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Lower-priced goods attract more customers说的是"低价商品吸引更多顾客"。原文 在加诱饵后的结果恰是"更多人选了更贵的"，并非低价更受欢迎；实验的核心是揭示诱 饵效应，不是廉价致胜。 B) ✓ 正确 the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option ↔The Economist's promotional strategy works 预判答案是"实验证明诱饵策略有效"，The Economist's promotional strategy works 里works即"奏效、起作用"，与预判中"有效"匹配；且promotional strategy恰好概括了 The Economist的特殊定价做法。 C) 与原文相反 The Economist's print edition turns out to sell the best说的是"纯纸质版卖得最 好"，但原文No one in their right mind would buy the print subscription when you could get digital as well for the same price明确指出几乎没人单买纸质版——它 根本不是最好卖的，而是诱饵本身。 D) 以偏概全 More readers choose the digital over the print edition说的是"更多读者选数字版而 非纸质版"。这只在But之前的场景（只有两个真实选项时）成立，But之后the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option改变了这个结果——而题问的是从整个实验中学到了什么，应 当看But之后的发现。 添加"劣选项"是为了什么目的? A) 为了迎合某些顾客的特殊需求。 B) 为了帮助顾客做出更理性的选择。 C) 为了诱使顾客购买价格更高的商品。 D) 为了给顾客提供更多样化的商品。

questions.q: For what purpose is "the bad option" (Line 7, Para. 3) added?
options: To cater to the peculiar needs of some customers.
To help customers to make more rational choices.
To trap customers into buying the more pricey item.
To provide customers with a greater variety of goods.
questions.explain:
【判型】For what purpose is "the bad option" added问的是文中明示的添加目的，是对原文信息 的客观转述，归为细节题。

【拆句】For what purpose is "the bad option" (Line 7, Para. 3) added?是被动疑问句，For what purpose是疑问短语前置，主语是the bad option，谓语是is added。括号内的Line 7, Para. 3是位置提示，不算原文成分。

【定位】But the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option. 但加入那个糟糕的选项使得人们更倾向于选择更贵的"纸质加数字"组合订阅。

【选项】A) 无中生有 To cater to the peculiar needs of some customers说的是"迎合某些顾客的特殊需 求"，但原文中加入诱饵的目的是营销操纵，不是为了满足顾客的任何需求；原文里No one in their right mind would buy the print subscription更直接说明没人需要这个 选项。 B) 与原文相反 To help customers to make more rational choices说的是"帮助顾客作出更理性的选 择"，但原文加入诱饵恰恰让顾客作出了非理性的选择——选了更贵的而非更便宜的；选 项把操纵动机说成助人为乐，方向反了。 C) ✓ 正确 made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option ↔ To trap customers into buying the more pricey item the more expensive print plus digital option ↔the more pricey item 预判答案为"使顾客买更贵的"，To trap customers into buying the more pricey item 里trap...into精准对应"诱饵"的负面操纵色彩，more pricey精准对应more expensive， 与预判完全匹配。 D) 偷换概念 To provide customers with a greater variety of goods说的是"为顾客提供更多种类的 商品"。原文中加诱饵不是为了丰富选项种类，而是为了利用对比心理把顾客推向最贵的 那个选项。 根据文章,我们如何评估商品的价值? A) 通过考虑它的实用性。 B) 通过将它与其他选择进行比较。 C) 通过将它的质量纳入考量。 D) 通过检查它的价值等式。

questions.q: How do we assess the value of a commodity, according to the passage?
options: By considering its usefulness.
By comparing it with other choices.
By taking its quality into account.
By examining its value equation.
questions.explain:
【判型】How do we assess the value of a commodity, according to the passage?末尾 according to the passage显式要求从文本中找答案，属细节题。

【拆句】How do we assess the value of a commodity, according to the passage?主干是How do we assess the value，of a commodity是修饰value的后置定语，according to the passage是插入语，表示信息来源。结构清晰。

【定位】Value is almost never absolute; rather, we decide an object's value relative to our other choices. 价值几乎从不是绝对的；而是说，我们是相对于自己拥有的其他选项来决定一个物品的 价值。

【选项】A) 无中生有 By considering its usefulness说的是"考虑其用处"，但原文Value is almost never absolute; rather, we decide an object's value relative to our other choices明确指出 价值是相对的，从未提到用处这个独立维度。 B) ✓ 正确 we decide an object's value relative to our other choices ↔ By comparing it with other choices decide an object's value ↔assess the value 预判答案为"相对于其他选项"，By comparing it with other choices的 comparing...with正是"相对"的动作化表达，与预判完全匹配。 C) 无中生有 By taking its quality into account说的是"将其质量纳入考量"，原文从头到尾未谈商品 质量；这是常识维度而非原文维度。 D) 偷换概念 By examining its value equation说的是"通过检视其价值等式"。原文If more options are introduced, the value equation changes里的value equation是对评估过程的命 名，不是用来评估的工具；选项把名词搬来制造熟悉，但用错了角色。
